entities.name: PMID:25074249
observations: 2014 split-belt treadmill study comparing 10 healthy adults and 20 adults post-stroke across tied-belt baseline, split-belt adaptation, and tied-belt post-adaptation.

Post-adaptation plantarflexion moment decreased for the fast limb and increased for the slow limb from mid-stance to toe-off in both groups; moment was significantly related to contralateral step length.

entities.name: Moment-step aftereffect association
observations: The study supports an association between plantarflexion moment and contralateral step length after split-belt adaptation in healthy and post-stroke participants; abstract-level evidence does not establish prediction or causation, nor a between-group difference in this relationship.
